one_line: A human-governed workbench where an agent can forge and test new WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect real data, propose a schema/body for a missing tool, test it against the data, obtain human grant, register it, and revoke it immediately.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic, human-approved tool creation inside the page changes the capability surface during the same conversation; a general UI-driving agent cannot comparably create and revoke typed page tools with shared state and an explicit grant boundary.
leverage_evidence: PITCH: lets an agent build the missing button and lets the person decide whether it keeps it.
ABOUT TEXT: forge_tool turns a name, JSON Schema, and JavaScript body into a real WebMCP tool only after human grant.
ABOUT TEXT: test run occurs before registration; Take it back aborts the signal and removes the tool immediately.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a detailed, coherent forge-test-grant-revoke loop and the frame sheet shows repeated workbench states, tables, controls, and side panels; exact tool execution remains only partially legible.
execution_evidence: FACTS: public_repo=True, demo_alive=alive, three video frame sheets submitted.
ABOUT TEXT: five permanent tools, pending unregistered state, editable code, test execution, grant and revocation.
raw/frames/w0TeuWbQV98/sheet1.jpg: repeated workbench states with changing controls and detail/activity panels.
impact_rationale: People and agents often encounter one-off workflow gaps where deploying a separate MCP server is disproportionate; safe local tool creation could unlock substantial practical utility.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT: current alternative requires writing/hosting an MCP server, editing config, and restarting the client.
ABOUT TEXT: operates against the user's real data with human approval.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic capability forging within the live page, coupled to a visible human grant and abortable lifecycle, is a genuinely novel and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: PITCH: build the one button missing.
ABOUT TEXT: agent reads real column names, forges a tool, tests it, then uses it in the same conversation; revocation is immediate.
usability_note: The visible workbench appears to expose pending code, status, controls, and activity detail, but readability and failure recovery are not fully verifiable at contact-sheet scale.
red_flags: Dynamic JavaScript tool bodies create a substantial security risk despite the human-grant boundary.
Frame text is too small to independently verify the complete loop.
standouts: A compelling capability lifecycle: inspect, forge, test, grant, invoke, revoke.
advance_reason: Most distinctive WebMCP concept in the packet, with unusually strong leverage and creativity and a credible safety lifecycle.
